display_name: Vasse Felix Filius Cabernet Sauvignon, Margaret River

The estate is a historic name in the region, and the Filius label is typically where the house style gets translated into a more accessible bottle: ripe black fruit, savory detail, and enough tannin to feel like Cabernet rather than anonymous dark red wine.\n\nPlace drives the profile. Margaret River’s long north-south strip along the southwestern cape is heavily shaped by ocean exposure, which moderates heat and stretches the growing season. That slower ripening is why Cabernet here can hold cassis, tobacco, mint, and dried herb notes together instead of veering into overripeness. The appellation’s red gravelly loam, loamy gravel over clay, deep infertile sand, and ironstone-heavy Forest Grove soils all tend to limit vine vigor in different ways; that matters because less vegetative growth usually means smaller berries and a higher skin-to-juice ratio, which translates into darker fruit concentration and more defined tannin.",

Deep infertile sands further curb vigor, and Forest Grove ironstone contributes to the region’s reputation for Cabernet with a ferrous, savory edge rather than simple fruit sweetness. That likely means controlled fermentation to extract color and tannin without drying the palate, followed by maturation in oak to round the tannins and add spice notes; tannin is the phenolic compound from grape skins, seeds, and wood that creates grip and gives Cabernet its ageability. parsed.hook: Margaret River Cabernet works because the region is maritime first, warm second: Indian and Southern Ocean influence keeps nights cooler and slows ripening, so blackcurrant flavor develops without pushing the wine into jammy territory. Filius sits in the smart-value tier of that formula, delivering the region’s calling card—cassis, bay leaf, mint, firm tannin—at a price where Napa and top Bordeaux blends usually can’t compete.
parsed.wine_summary:
This wine matters because Margaret River is Australia’s clearest answer to Cabernet with structure and freshness, and Vasse Felix is central to that story. The estate is a historic name in the region, and the Filius label is typically where the house style gets translated into a more accessible bottle: ripe black fruit, savory detail, and enough tannin to feel like Cabernet rather than anonymous dark red wine.

Place drives the profile. Margaret River’s long north-south strip along the southwestern cape is heavily shaped by ocean exposure, which moderates heat and stretches the growing season. That slower ripening is why Cabernet here can hold cassis, tobacco, mint, and dried herb notes together instead of veering into overripeness. The appellation’s red gravelly loam, loamy gravel over clay, deep infertile sand, and ironstone-heavy Forest Grove soils all tend to limit vine vigor in different ways; that matters because less vegetative growth usually means smaller berries and a higher skin-to-juice ratio, which translates into darker fruit concentration and more defined tannin.
parsed.terroir_expression: Red gravelly loam and loamy gravel over clay are classic Cabernet ground because gravel improves drainage and makes vines work harder, while clay underneath can hold enough moisture to prevent shutdown in warm periods. In Margaret River, that sits under a maritime climate with consistent ocean influence, reducing extreme heat spikes and preserving acid. Deep infertile sands further curb vigor, and Forest Grove ironstone contributes to the region’s reputation for Cabernet with a ferrous, savory edge rather than simple fruit sweetness. In the glass, that combination reads as dense blackberry and cassis framed by mint, nori, tobacco, and spice, with tannins that feel structural rather than coarse.
parsed.vinification_summary: The exact cépage and élevage details are not provided here, so limited technical specificity is possible. What fits both the wine’s profile and Vasse Felix’s regional style is a Cabernet-led red made to preserve fruit definition and savory complexity rather than overwhelm it with oak. That likely means controlled fermentation to extract color and tannin without drying the palate, followed by maturation in oak to round the tannins and add spice notes; tannin is the phenolic compound from grape skins, seeds, and wood that creates grip and gives Cabernet its ageability. The supple mid-palate noted by critics suggests extraction was managed carefully, not pushed for brute force.
food_pairing: Nashville hot chicken — the wine’s cassis fruit and firm tannin stand up to the chili heat, while its minty, savory edge cools the palate better than a softer red would.
Lamb kofta with sumac yogurt and charred eggplant — Cabernet’s dark fruit and tobacco notes match the lamb’s richness, and the yogurt softens the tannin.
Cheeseburger with aged cheddar and caramelized onions — this is a strong casual pairing because the protein and fat tame the tannins, while the wine’s herbal notes keep the burger from feeling heavy.
Pepper-crusted venison loin with blackberry jus — the wine’s dense blackberry, cassis, and spice mirror the sauce, and the game meat brings out the region’s savory, ironstone-like side.

Dry-aged ribeye with rosemary roasted potatoes — classic for a reason: fat buffers tannin, char picks up the wine’s tobacco and palo santo notes, and rosemary connects with the Cabernet’s mint-herb profile.
comparable_wines: Cullen Mangan Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon — comparable because it offers the same Margaret River mix of cassis, herbal lift, and marine-influenced freshness, usually with a bit more restraint.
Xanadu Circa 77 Cabernet Sauvignon — similar regional value play, with Margaret River blackcurrant fruit, bay leaf notes, and firm but approachable structure.

Chateau Ste. Michelle Indian Wells Cabernet Sauvignon — comparable in price and accessibility, though riper and softer; useful as a contrast if you want to see how Margaret River keeps more herbal freshness and shape.
parsed.style_profile: Full-bodied dry red with firm tannins and savory maritime Cabernet character
parsed.cellar_recommendation: Drink the current release now through about 6-8 years from vintage for best balance of fruit and secondary notes. Store at a stable cool temperature away from light; this is structured enough to reward short-term cellaring but built more for confident mid-term drinking than for decades.
parsed.value_assessment: $26.31 puts this in a very competitive Cabernet slot, and it clears the bar. At that price, it sits against wines like Coonawarra staples from Wynns and value Napa-adjacent bottlings such as Louis M. Martini Sonoma County Cabernet, but this offers a more savory, region-specific profile than many similarly priced international Cabernets. It is worth buying because you get real Margaret River typicity—cassis, mint, structure, freshness—without paying estate-flagship money.
parsed.market_position: This is aimed at drinkers who want a serious Cabernet for weeknight steak, not a trophy bottle for the cellar. It belongs on independent retail shelves, by-the-bottle restaurant lists, and Australian-focused programs where buyers want regional identity under $30. Collectors will look higher up the Vasse Felix range, but informed casual drinkers and sommeliers looking for value should pay attention here.
parsed.insider_take: Think of this as the bottle for people who say they want Cabernet with flavor, not syrup. The tradeoff is clear: you get structure, herb lift, and savory detail instead of plush sweetness, so drinkers chasing soft, mocha-heavy Cabernet should skip it. What many buyers miss is that this tier still carries the Margaret River signature clearly; it is not a diluted brand extension.
